items.stem: Why does Terraform keep a state file?

options.text: To map real infrastructure to your configuration and detect changes
options.rationale: Correct: state records what Terraform manages so it can compute diffs.

options.text: To store your cloud provider password
options.rationale: State is not a credential store; credentials come from provider configuration.

options.text: To compile the configuration into a binary
options.rationale: Terraform does not compile config to a binary.
State has nothing to do with documentation.

items.explanation: Correct: state records what Terraform manages so it can compute diffs.

options.rationale: Correct: plan computes and displays the proposed changes without applying.
init prepares the working directory and downloads providers.

items.stem: Which TWO practices are recommended for Terraform state in a team? (Select TWO)

options.text: Store state in a remote backend with locking
options.rationale: Correct: remote state with locking prevents concurrent conflicting applies.

options.text: Avoid committing state files containing secrets to version control
options.rationale: Correct: state can hold sensitive values and should not be in a public repo.

options.text: Let every engineer keep their own local state copy of shared infra
options.rationale: Divergent local states cause conflicts and drift.

options.text: Edit the state file by hand to fix most problems
options.rationale: Manual edits are error-prone; use state commands instead.
